data.summary: The two‑week plan front‑loads the weak Integration unit while giving a broad sweep of the entire AP Calculus AB curriculum. Week 1 introduces core concepts and intensive practice, especially on Unit 6. Week 2 is a mixed review and timed practice session covering all units to solidify knowledge before the exam.

weeks.focus: Build foundational skills and strengthen Unit 6 (Integration and Accumulation of Change).
tasks: Do 15 limit‑evaluation problems (1.1‑1.5) and check answers with the solution key.
Complete 12 derivative‑definition exercises (2.1‑2.2) and verify using the power rule (2.5).
Work through 6 related‑rates scenarios (4.4) and write the full set‑up for each.
Practice 10 Mean Value/Extreme Value theorem questions (5.1‑5.2).
Complete the Riemann‑sum worksheet: 5 approximations for 6.2, write the summation notation for 6.3, and evaluate a definite integral using the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (6.4).
Time yourself: 20 mixed‑topic free‑response questions covering topics above; grade with the AP scoring guide.

weeks.focus: Mixed review and timed practice of all units.
tasks: Review graph‑based limit estimation (1.3‑1.4) with 10 practice graphs.
Do 12 derivative‑application problems (2.3‑2.4) focusing on continuity and differentiability.
Solve 6 motion‑context problems linking position, velocity, and acceleration (4.2‑4.3).
Analyze 10 functions for increasing/decreasing intervals and apply the First Derivative Test (5.3‑5.4).
Model 5 differential‑equation situations, verify solutions, and sketch slope fields (7.1‑7.4).
Finish 8 integration‑application tasks: average value, area between curves, and applied accumulation (8.1‑8.4).
Take a full 90‑minute timed practice exam, then compare answers to the official scoring guidelines.

data.final_week_advice: After the timed practice, review any missed questions, focus on the underlying concepts that caused errors, and do a quick 30‑minute refresher of key formulas and theorems before the exam day.
